subject: CloudLogger onboarding: subprocessor change + DPA redline
messages:
From: Samantha Reeves <samantha@cloudlogger.io>
To: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudLogger Ops <ops@cloudlogger.io>
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: addition of LogStream as subprocessor (long-term logs)

Hi Chloe —

Quick heads-up: CloudLogger is planning to route longer-term log retention (30+ days) to a third-party storage processor, LogStream, starting July 1. This is to reduce our S3 egress and enable our analytics tier.

Attached is the current subprocessor register and a short summary of the scope. At a glance: LogStream will receive only structured application logs (no PII) and they will perform encrypted-at-rest cold storage and index generation.

Can you confirm the flowdown we need for Redwood’s MSA/order form? If you prefer, we can provide a brief subprocessor agreement and SOC2 report snapshot.

Attachments: CloudLogger-Subproc-list.xlsx (XLSX)

Thanks,
Samantha Reeves
Head of Ops, CloudLogger
[Attachment: CloudLogger-Subproc-list.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Reeves <samantha@cloudlogger.io>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: addition of LogStream as subprocessor (long-term logs)

Thanks for the alert, Samantha — and for the register. A few clarifying asks from our side so we can determine whether this is a material change under our MSA and what DPA/order-form work is required: 

- Can you confirm whether LogStream will ever receive any user identifiers (email, customer_id) or whether logs are strictly app-level event streams with hashed ids?
- Please share a current SOC 2 report (or SOC 2 Type II snapshot) and the identity/access controls for their engineers (SRE roles) who will have log access.
- Retention: you mentioned 30+ days — what is the default retention and are there customer-configurable retention windows?
- Encryption: confirm keys (CloudLogger-managed KMS vs LogStream-managed keys) and whether Redwood has any ability to enforce encryption at rest for our data class.

Cc'ing Lauren for legal gating and Dev for technical gating. If this is PII-exempt we may route a simple subprocessor notification and updated annex; if not, we will need DPA redlines and potentially an Order Form amendment.

Next steps: please drop the SOC2 link and a proposed subprocessor agreement; we’ll triage internally and get back with specific redline requests.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Manager, Customer Ops — Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Samantha Reeves <samantha@cloudlogger.io>
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: addition of LogStream as subprocessor (long-term logs)

Chloe — quick legal checklist and routing: 

- If LogStream will process any personal data tied to our customers, treat this as a material subprocessor change requiring either (a) explicit customer notice/consent under certain DPAs, or (b) confirmation that the original DPA already permits this subdelegation.
- Request CloudLogger to provide: (i) granular subprocessor agreement that includes flowdown of data controller/processor obligations; (ii) a redline of our standard DPA to show proposed changes to subprocessors clause; (iii) export controls/KYC of LogStream (if they store cross-border).
- DocuSign path: if Order Form amendments are needed (e.g., new subprocessor fees or SLA changes), we’ll route an amendment via DocuSign and notify Acme legal.

Please mark this as high priority for Acme Health (account impact) and route any vendor DPA redlines to me directly. I’ll prepare a short memo for the privacy review group.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

On Sat, Apr 19, 2025 at 08:47 AM CloudLogger Ops <ops@cloudlogger.io> wrote:
From: CloudLogger Ops <ops@cloudlogger.io>
To: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Reeves <samantha@cloudlogger.io>, elliot.price@acmehealth.com
Date: Sat, 19 Apr 2025 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: addition of LogStream as subprocessor (long-term logs)

Hi Chloe —

Thanks for the questions — please see answers below and attached redline: 

- PII: LogStream will not receive cleartext PII. We’ll send logs with hashed identifiers and remove any user-email fields at ingestion.
- SOC2: LogStream provided a current SOC2 Type II snapshot (redacted) here: https://logstream.com/soc2/redacted (password: LS2025).
- Retention: default 90 days; can be configured per-customer to 30/90/365.
- Encryption: data encrypted at rest with customer-managed KMS optional. By default, CloudLogger manages keys; if Redwood requires, we can enable bring-your-own-key for your account.

Attached: CloudLogger-DPA-redline.pdf (highlights: subprocessors clause and cross-border clause)
Attached: CloudLogger-Subproc-list.xlsx

We’ve also included a proposed subprocessor addendum that LogStream has countersigned for operational controls — happy to route the signed addendum if you want it as evidence.

Let us know if you need us to remove LogStream from the onboarding for Acme while you triage.

Best,
CloudLogger Ops
[Attachment: CloudLogger-DPA-redline.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: CloudLogger-Subproc-list.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: CloudLogger Ops <ops@cloudlogger.io>, chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Apr 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: addition of LogStream as subprocessor (long-term logs)

Samantha / CloudLogger — quick technical follow-ups so our infra team can sign off: 

1) Access controls: confirm whether LogStream engineers will be able to query logs via a console or only through API with scoped tokens. We need role scoping examples.
2) KMS integration: if we enable BYOK, who owns the KMS keys and what IAM principals are required? Provide an example IAM policy.
3) Data minimization: can you provide the exact schema transformation pipeline that strips user_email and how you guarantee no PII remains (e.g., regex scrub + redaction logs)?
4) Deletion/retain: if a customer requests deletion, how fast can LogStream purge cold storage? SLA target?

If CloudLogger can share a short tech note for our infra reviewers, we’ll expedite.

Thanks — Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Engineer, Runtime Reliability

From: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Reeves <samantha@cloudlogger.io>, CloudLogger Ops <ops@cloudlogger.io>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, elliot.price@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 20 Apr 2025 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: addition of LogStream as subprocessor (long-term logs)

Team — internal summary and next steps for Acme Health account: 

Summary: CloudLogger proposes to add LogStream as a cold-storage subprocessor (default 90d retention). Vendor supplied DPA redline and SOC2 snapshot; they offer BYOK. Vendor asserts no cleartext PII is shared.

Internal action items (owners):
- Lauren: review CloudLogger-DPA-redline.pdf and produce a one-page redline summary and required edits for our DPA flowdown (due 2025-04-23).
- Dev: review technical note from CloudLogger (access controls, BYOK, deletion SLA) and confirm whether retention options and BYOK are acceptable (due 2025-04-22).
- Chloe: coordinate an Order Form amendment if Lauren’s review requires a signed flowdown or fees change; I will prepare DocuSign routing and notify Acme legal.

External ask to CloudLogger (please provide by 2025-04-22):
1) Final redlined DPA (PDF) with tracked changes + a clean final version for DocuSign.
2) Tech note addressing Dev’s 4 bullets (access controls, KMS/BYOK sample policy, schema scrub details, deletion SLA).
3) Copies of any signed subprocessor addendum for LogStream (evidence).

If CloudLogger prefers, we can pause LogStream onboarding for Acme until we finish the triage — please confirm.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Senior Manager, Customer Ops — Redwood Inference
